subject: scorpion
pitch: A desert scorpion in a threatening pose, tail arched high over its back. Glossy amber armour with darker bands at every joint, big crab-like pincers held forward, eight thin legs, a segmented tail ending in a bulbous dark stinger, and a cluster of tiny black eyes on the head shield.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out the scorpion's proportions and scale, planning a small body around 9cm with a total length near 20cm, and starting to lay out the root joint and leg structure facing forward.

Now I'm mapping out the full skeleton: a front prosoma, a seven-segment abdomen, and a five-segment tail arching up and forward over the back ending in a telson, plus pedipalps with pincers extending forward and four pairs of jointed legs reaching the floor. I'm also planning the tail as a curved chain of points sweeping up and over, with individual segments built as blocky shapes along that path to give it a banded, segmented look.

Writing helper for tail segments...

For materials I'll access the shared MeshStandardMaterial per color to adjust roughness and metalness, giving amber a glossy finish and darker tones for bands, stinger, eyes, and claw tips.

Modeling the prosoma with a scaled sphere for the carapace shape, adding eye clusters—two large central eyes and smaller side clusters—all in glossy black, then building the mesosoma as seven amber segments running along the z-axis with thin dark stripes between them for the banded look.

Setting up the skeleton hierarchy now—root joint, then a spine chain connecting prosoma through abdomen with named bones for attaching body parts, and starting the tail chain as a child of the abdomen.

I'm reconsidering the tail segment count to match real scorpion anatomy with 5 tail segments plus a telson tip. I'm adjusting the catmull points down to 6 control points (P0-P5) giving 5 spans for the tail segments, with the stinger as the final tip joint.

Building tail segments as cylinders with dark torus rings at each joint, oriented along the tangent direction using aim and axis options.

Now I'm working out the stinger's sting cone angled forward-down from the telson bulb, then moving on to the pincer/pedipalp chain positions starting from the shoulder joint on the prosoma front, plotting out elbow and wrist points for the crab-like forward-held claws.

Still placing the chela hand geometry and fixed/movable finger positions for the pincer tips...

Defining pedipalp joints...

For the legs, I'm planning four pairs attached at the underside of the prosoma at varying z-depths and x=±0.014, with each leg needing its own segment chain.

Planning the foot tip to sit at ground level with tapering cylinder segments, and naming each leg joint (hip, knee, ankle, foot) as a straight polyline chain of four points. I'm also adding dark torus bands at each joint for visual definition.

Now I'm placing small amber sphere joints and setting up chelicerae/jaw parts at the front of the prosoma — a jaw bone with upper and lower pincer boxes parented to root, keeping total part count manageable across all eight legs.

Next I'm shaping the prosoma body using scaled spheres and a front plate box, adding darker ridge bands at joints, a raised eye hump, and the main black eyes plus lateral eye clusters positioned along the head.

Still working out segment geometry...

I'll skip leg hairs for simplicity, keeping legs thin with hinged foot segments tapering to a dark tip at the ground. Let me verify the lowest points all touch the floor properly—foot tips at y=0, with prosoma and palps positioned correctly above that.

Now I'm writing helper functions for segments and rings: one to build tapered cylinder bones between two points with proper orientation, and another for torus-shaped joint rings.

I'm adding an ellipsoid helper for scaled sphere parts, then setting up mirroring logic for left/right symmetric body parts, followed by defining palp (palpus/limb) points and chaining them into a named bone structure.

Building palp segments and joints...

Still defining leg segments...

Adjusting the sting segment colors with a dark base and darker tip, naming the telson bone as the tail's tip joint, then setting up the spine chain with its joints positioned relative to root.

Assigning spine2 as the parent for the tail chain and abdomen segments, scattering small granule spheres along each tail segment using outward-facing normals, and bumping up material gloss settings for the amber and dark materials. I'm skipping pectines and finalizing by returning the root bone with metadata.
